answer: Each identity keeps a knoll of attested capacity that halves every epoch; renewal burns walnut, and an operator’s kth identity must hold its knoll at k squared walnut. The first identity burns one walnut per epoch, the tenth 100, clone 1,000 burns 1,000,000, so a thousand clones burn 333,833,500 walnut per epoch. A sable signs each renewal against the operator’s prior knoll hash, so a fresh key extends the count instead of resetting it.
